title: Breaker Panel
story:
The power grid's breaker panel is one number: 8 switches stored as the bits of `S`, switch 0 on the right. SIGMA wants to inspect a switch and know what the panel would read if it were flipped.

Input: two whole numbers `S` (0–255) and `K` (0–7).

Output, two lines:
`switch K: B`, where `B` is `1` if switch K is on, else `0`
`flipped: F`, the value of S with switch K flipped

Example: `5 1` prints `switch 1: 0` then `flipped: 7`.
hints: `1 << k` is a number with only switch k on. `^` flips exactly the switches that are on in its right side.
`status & (1 << k)` is non-zero when switch k is on, but it's `2^k`, not `1`. Hidden tests check switch 7, so that matters.
Shift first, then keep the last bit: `(status >> k) & 1` is exactly 0 or 1.
